body: ## Investors Take Some Chips Off the Table as Rally Broadens Out. Selling pressure continued in the tech sector as investors rotate out of the momentum trade into other areas of the market. ## The Week That Was. If you read last week's blog, you might recall that I had a "Moderately Bearish" forecast on the technology sector this week, citing concerns around quarter-end rebalancing and signs of speculative excess (stretched margin debt) and concentrated positioning in the AI infrastructure cohort of the market. The PHLX Semiconductor Index (SOX) is down 12% over the last two days, in part due to a sharp overnight drop (-7.89%) in the Korea Composite Stock Price Index (KOSPI). The near-term technicals look bifurcated from my lens–the S&P Equal Weight Index (SPXEW), Russel 2000 (RUT), and Dow Jones Industrial Average (DJI) look bullish, but the Nasdaq Composite ($COMP) is dropping back below its 50-day Simple Moving Average (SMA) today, and the SOX firmly broke its uptrend today (more on this in the "Technical Take" section below).
